title: JDK dynamic proxies and CGLIB
context: What is the difference between JDK dynamic proxies and CGLIB proxies?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A JDK dynamic proxy implements the interfaces of a target object at run time through `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`. It works only when the target implements an interface. CGLIB creates a subclass of the target class at run time, so it works for classes without interfaces, but it can't proxy final classes or final methods. Spring Boot uses CGLIB by default. Both are used by Spring AOP for transactions and aspects.

points.title: Interface versus subclass
points.why: JDK proxies need an interface. CGLIB needs a class that isn't final.

points.title: Final members
points.why: Final classes and methods can't be overridden, so they can't be intercepted.
